grammarPoints.subject: english
grammarPoints.title: Passive with modals
grammarPoints.rule: Use a modal — must, must not, have to, can, can't — plus be plus the past participle to say what has to or can be done to something.

chart.title: Passive with modals

intro_examples.text: Headlamps must be worn in dark caves.
intro_examples.jp: 暗い洞窟ではヘッドランプを身につけなければなりません。

intro_examples.text: Dangerous places must not be entered alone.
intro_examples.jp: 危険な場所に一人で入ってはいけません。

intro_examples.text: New species have to be studied in a science lab.
intro_examples.jp: 新種は科学の研究室で調べなければなりません。

rows.example: Headlamps must be worn in dark caves.
rows.jp: 暗い洞窟ではヘッドランプを身につけなければなりません。

rows.pattern: subject + must not be + past participle
rows.example: Dangerous places must not be entered alone.
rows.jp: 危険な場所に一人で入ってはいけません。

rows.pattern: subject + have to be + past participle
rows.example: New species have to be studied in a science lab.
rows.jp: 新種は科学の研究室で調べなければなりません。
それらは水中では分析できません。

rows.example: A rope can be used to help us descend.
rows.jp: ロープは降りるのを助けるために使えます。

chart.note_rule: Be never changes after a modal — only the past participle tells you what is done.
chart.note_exception: Must not means it is forbidden. Can't means it is impossible.
chart.note_exception_detail: Have to changes for the subject (has to be studied for a singular subject) but must never changes.

table.title: modal + be + past participle
notes: Be always stays as be after a modal.

grammarPoints.subject: english
grammarPoints.title: Make + someone + adjective
grammarPoints.rule: Use make + a person + an adjective to say what causes a feeling. The adjective describes the person, not the thing.

chart.title: Make + someone + adjective

intro_examples.jp: 洞窟は私を怖がらせます。
探検はミレヤを幸せにします。
高い場所は彼女を不安にさせました。

rows.jp: 洞窟は私を怖がらせます。
探検はミレヤを幸せにします。
高い場所は彼女を不安にさせました。

rows.pattern: make + me / him / her / us / them + adjective
rows.jp: それは私をとても怒らせます。

rows.pattern: never say make me to be scared
rows.jp: make me to be scared とは言いません。

chart.note_rule: The thing that causes the feeling is the subject; the person who feels it is the object.
chart.note_exception: Use an object pronoun after make: me, him, her, us, them — never I, he, she.
chart.note_exception_detail: There is no to and no be: say it makes me happy, not it makes me to be happy.

table.title: make + object + adjective
notes: Use makes with a singular subject and make with a plural one.
